title: How Reliable Are System-One Decisions in Medicine? A Comparative Study of Jev, Jev-like Models, and LLMs
abstract: arXiv:2610.18529v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Jev has attracted considerable attention for its rapid, generalizable decision-making, yet its medical reliability remains underexplored. To address this gap, our study compares various types of system-one decision models across 15 medical datasets comprising 8,742 instances under a unified protocol. Beyond accuracy, we assess decision stability and the ability to recognize unreliable decisions. Our results show that Jev rivals leading models on primarily text-driven tasks but is less effective on numerically driven tasks, revealing a distinct capability boundary. Under question-format variations, Jev maintains strong decision consistency and small accuracy fluctuations. StartLux-27B exhibits comparable consistency, while D3-27B achieves higher overall accuracy and a lower mean decision reversal rate. translated_title: 医学中“系统一”决策的可靠性如何？Jev、类Jev模型与大语言模型的对比研究
translated_abstract: Jev因其快速且可泛化的决策能力而受到广泛关注，但其在医学领域的可靠性仍未得到充分研究。为填补这一空白，本研究在统一协议下，于包含8,742个实例的15个医学数据集上比较了多种类型的系统一决策模型。除准确率之外，我们还评估了决策稳定性以及识别不可靠决策的能力。结果显示，Jev在以文本为主的任务上可与领先模型相媲美，但在以数值为主的任务上表现较弱，揭示了其明确的能力边界。在问题格式发生变化的情形下，Jev保持了较强的决策一致性和较小的准确率波动。StartLux-27B表现出相当的决策一致性，而D3-27B则取得了更高的整体准确率和更低的平均决策反转率。然而，这些优势并未延伸到可靠的弃权意识（abstention awareness）上：大多数受评估模型在识别缺失信息方面均存在局限。
tldr: 本研究在15个医学数据集上系统对比了Jev、类Jev模型与大语言模型，发现Jev在文本驱动任务上表现优异且决策一致性强，但在数值驱动任务上存在明显能力边界，且多数模型在识别缺失信息、实现可靠弃权方面仍有不足。
en_tdlr: This study systematically compares Jev, Jev-like models, and LLMs across 15 medical datasets, showing that Jev rivals leading models on text-driven tasks with strong decision consistency but faces a distinct capability boundary on numerically driven tasks, while most models remain limited in reliable abstention awareness.
